title: Levodopa kinetic-dynamic test
author: Manuela Contin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbq8imzw

steps.title: Prepare Patient for Dosing
steps.instruction: Ensure the patient is under standardized conditions prior to administration.

substeps.instruction: Ensure a fasting state for dosing.
Ensure a wash-out period of at least 12 hours for levodopa and any concomitant antiparkinsonian therapy.

steps.title: Administer Levodopa Test Dose
steps.instruction: Administer a subacute test dose of levodopa (100 mg) plus either benserazide (25 mg) or carbidopa (25 mg).

steps.title: Collect Blood Samples
steps.instruction: Draw blood samples using an indwelling catheter according to the specified timeline.

substeps.instruction: Draw a baseline sample before levodopa dosing.
Draw samples at 15-min intervals for the first 90 min post-dosing.
Draw samples half-hourly from 90 min up to 3 hours post-dosing.

steps.title: Process and Store Plasma
steps.instruction: Prepare plasma samples from blood specimens for analysis.

substeps.instruction: Transfer blood specimens into heparinized tubes.
Immediately centrifuge tubes at 1500 g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Store plasma samples at −80°C until analysis (typically within 6 months).

steps.title: Measure Levodopa Plasma Concentration
steps.instruction: Perform measurements of levodopa plasma concentration using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) with coulometric detection.

steps.title: Test Motor Effects
steps.instruction: Evaluate motor effects up to 4 hours post-dosing using a computerized touch screen system (mTapping, mHealth Technologies srl, Bologna, Italy).

substeps.instruction: Perform the alternate index finger tapping test by counting how many times the patient can alternately tap two buttons 20 cm apart in 60 seconds with the most affected hand.

steps.title: Rate Levodopa Induced Dyskinesias
steps.instruction: Rate possible levodopa induced dyskinesias using the Clinical Dyskinesia Rating Scale (CDRS) at the same time points as the motor response tests.
